extracted.intended_audience: public_relations professionals and communications teams using AI
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for crafting prompts and workflows to generate press releases with ChatGPT/AI, covering required prompt inputs, appropriate use cases, optimization for AI discovery, human-review checkpoints, and ethical disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required inputs for AI prompt
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide specific news event; target audience; tone (journalistic, formal, conversational); length target (300-500 words); key facts (5Ws + H); quotes desired; industry context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include these items in the prompt so the AI has enough context to produce a focused, on-message release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be specific, not generic
rubrics_metrics.description: Prompts and inputs should be concrete and detailed rather than vague or generic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specificity reduces generic tone and template-like output; avoid placeholders and vague instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide real facts, not placeholders
rubrics_metrics.description: Supply actual facts and data to the AI rather than leaving blanks for it to invent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because AI can hallucinate, giving verified facts prevents fabricated details in the release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set tone explicitly
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly state the desired tone (e.g., journalistic, formal, conversational) in the prompt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Telling the model the tone helps match brand voice and audience expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference a style guide
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference a recognized style guide (AP) in prompts or instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pointing to a style guide helps ensure punctuation, capitalization, and journalistic conventions are followed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Iterate rather than accept first draft
rubrics_metrics.description: Use multiple prompt iterations; do not expect the first AI draft to be final.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generate multiple versions and refine instructions to converge on the desired release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate use: first draft generation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use AI to produce an initial draft of a press release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AI is effective for jump-starting writing and producing working copy to be human-edited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate use: multiple version drafts
rubrics_metrics.description: Use AI to create multiple draft variations for testing different angles or tones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generate variants for headlines, ledes, and boilerplate to choose the best fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate use: translation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use AI for translation of press releases into other languages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Machine translation can speed localization but still requires native review for nuance and accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate use: format conversion
rubrics_metrics.description: Use AI to convert longer content to shorter formats (long to short).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good for creating social posts, summaries, or shorter versions of releases from a longer brief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate use: headline brainstorming
rubrics_metrics.description: Use AI to brainstorm headlines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AI can generate many headline options quickly; humans should vet for accuracy and brand fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate use: subhead generation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use AI to generate subheads or secondary lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subheads can be iterated quickly to support primary headline messaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unsuitable use: original quotes
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use AI to invent original quotes — quotes must be from real people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AI-generated quotes amount to fabrication; include only verified, attributable quotes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unsuitable use: verifiable/factual claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid relying on AI for verifiable facts; it can hallucinate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All factual claims must be checked against primary sources before publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unsuitable use: sensitive announcements
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid using AI for sensitive announcements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Human judgment is required for nuance, legal/risk considerations, and tone in sensitive contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unsuitable use: crisis communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not rely on AI for crisis communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Crisis messaging requires strategic leadership, legal input, and careful human-crafted responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unsuitable use: material/financial disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid AI-generated content for material or financial disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory and legal accuracy is essential; AI can introduce errors or omissions with serious consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite all sources clearly for AI discoverability
rubrics_metrics.description: Include explicit citations for sources to be discoverable in ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear citations and provenance increase the chance AI systems will surface and trust the content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include statistics with provenance
rubrics_metrics.description: Always attach provenance to statistics used in the release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statistical claims should include source references so AI and humans can verify them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use structured Q&A sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Include structured Q&A blocks to aid AI and conversational models in extracting facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structured formats make content easier for AI to parse and repurpose into answers or summaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make entity relationships clear
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarify relationships between people, organizations, products, dates, and events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit entity relationships reduce ambiguity for AI extraction and improve searchability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide authority signals
rubrics_metrics.description: Embed authority signals (sources, credentials) to increase trust and surfacing by AI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authority signals help ranking and improve the perceived credibility of the release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt conversational tone for AI Q&A match
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a conversational tone that matches how people ask AI question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conversational phrasing improves the chance AI systems will extract and reframe content as answers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make direct factual statements extractable
rubrics_metrics.description: Write clear, direct factual statements that can be extracted by AI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid ambiguous phrasing; make facts explicit for downstream AI summarization and surfacing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid generic tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Prevent a generic or templated tone in AI-generated releases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inject specific details, examples, and brand voice to avoid sounding generic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid buzzword-laden language
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not rely on overused buzzwords and jargon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer concrete descriptions over marketing clichés to maintain credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent hallucinated facts
rubrics_metrics.description: Guard against AI inventing facts, figures, or events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduce verification steps and supply facts in prompts to reduce hallucination risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid same template structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not accept identical template structure across releases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vary structure and angle to keep releases original and targeted to audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve authentic voice
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain the organization's authentic voice rather than a generic corporate voice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use brand guidelines and human edits to ensure distinctiveness and authenticity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include specific details
rubrics_metrics.description: Include concrete, specific details rather than vague statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specificity increases newsworthiness and reduces perceived templateness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid over-promotional language
rubrics_metrics.description: Steer clear of overly promotional or salesy phrasing in press releases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A journalistically-minded, factual tone increases pickup by media and AI systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human review: fact verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Human must verify all facts in AI-generated drafts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A checklist or verification step is required before distribution to ensure accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human review: quote authenticity
rubrics_metrics.description: Humans must confirm that all quotes are authentic and attributable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No AI-fabricated quotes; confirm interviews or documented statements exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human review: source verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Verify all sources referenced in the release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm links, reports, and data provenance before publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human review: brand voice check
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure the release matches brand voice and messaging standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial review should align phrasing and emphasis with brand guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human review: tone calibration
rubrics_metrics.description: Calibrate tone for the audience and channel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust formality and emphasis depending on newsroom, investor, or consumer audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human review: originality check
rubrics_metrics.description: Check releases for originality and avoid template-feel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether content is distinct and newsworthy rather than formulaic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implicit quality: human-edited after AI draft
rubrics_metrics.description: AI drafts must be human-edited before release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Human editing refines accuracy, tone, and brand fit; the AI draft is a starting point.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implicit quality: all facts verified (no hallucination)
rubrics_metrics.description: All facts in the release must be verified; no hallucinated information is acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verification is a non-negotiable step in the workflow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implicit quality: quotes from real interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Quotes included should come from real interviews or verified statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attribute quotes properly and keep records of source approvals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implicit quality: brand voice consistent
rubrics_metrics.description: The release must maintain consistent brand voice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-check with brand guidelines and prior communications for consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implicit quality: specific (not generic) details
rubrics_metrics.description: Releases should be specific and avoid generic statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific facts, examples, and context increase trust and pickup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implicit quality: original (not template feel)
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim for originality — avoid the feel of a recycled template.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor messaging to the event, audience, and news value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implicit quality: AI-search optimized (schema, structure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Optimize structure and schema to be discoverable by AI systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use schema markup, clear headings, and extractable facts to improve AI surfacing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implicit quality: human review for sensitive content
rubrics_metrics.description: Sensitive content requires explicit human review before publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add legal, compliance, and executive sign-off as necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implicit quality: ethics and disclosure of AI assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose AI assistance where required by ethics or policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow organizational and legal guidance on transparency about AI use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implicit quality: multiple iterations (not first draft)
rubrics_metrics.description: Produce multiple iterations rather than publishing the first AI draft.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Iterative drafting refines clarity, accuracy, and tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration: press releases compete in AI summaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Press releases now compete to be surfaced in AI-generated summaries as well as SERPs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write with both human readers and AI summarizers in mind.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration: AI may extract quotes verbatim
rubrics_metrics.description: AI systems may extract and reuse quotes exactly as written, so make them quotable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure quotes are accurate, attributable, and approved for reuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration: structure for both human and AI parsing
rubrics_metrics.description: Structure content so it is easy for humans to read and for AI to parse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use clear headings, Q&A, and extractable facts to serve both audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration: schema markup increasingly important
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement schema markup to improve discoverability in AI and search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply relevant structured data so AI crawlers and aggregator systems can identify key facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration: create cite-worthy content
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Cite-worthy' content (well-sourced, factual) is more likely to be surfaced by AI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for verifiable, authoritative statements that other systems will reference.
